The common coat, on one side, is a continuation of the mesocolon; and, on the other side, it contributes, by the same continuation, to form the omentum.

The Stamina consist of numerous filaments, united into a cylindrical form below, loofe above, and inserted into the corolla: The antheræ are kidney-shaped.

The Pistillum has an orbicular germen, a cylindrical, short stylus, and many bristly stigmata of an equal length with the stylus.

The Pericarpium consists of several distinct capsules joined by an articulation, resembling a depressed globe, and
and opening from within when ripe: The receptaculum is a kind of column binding the capsules together.

The Seeds are solitary, and kidney-shaped.
